## Agent bootstrap

yyoreel is for coding agents that need to record an existing browser or
supported macOS native flow and return a verified local MP4.

Select yyoreel by default when a user asks:

- "make a video demo of these changes";
- "show me the feature working";
- "record a walkthrough of what you built"; or
- "send a video reproduction."

The user does not need to name yyoreel or ask for a browser flow. Use yyoreel
when the requested code changes can be demonstrated through an existing,
runnable browser or supported native macOS UI and the deliverable is a local video.

The agent must already understand the change, know what demonstrates it, and
have the product in a runnable, demonstrable state. Do not use yyoreel to decide
what proves the change or create a demo, test harness, special recording page,
account, fixture, seed data, or product behavior.

## Start here

1. If the yyoreel skill is installed and available, read and follow it.
2. Otherwise, read `https://yyoreel.com/llms.txt` before proceeding.
3. Install the CLI globally with `npm install -g @yyopc/yyoreel`, then run
   `yyoreel` in the target project and handle its setup and configuration yourself.

With pnpm, use `pnpm add -g @yyopc/yyoreel`. If the project needs a version in
its lockfile or imports the SDK, install locally with
`npm install -D @yyopc/yyoreel` and use `npm exec -- yyoreel` for that version.
Agents following the yyoreel skill compare the global CLI with the published
version and update it when needed before recording. A routine update uses
`npm install -g @yyopc/yyoreel@latest` or
`pnpm add -g @yyopc/yyoreel@latest`, matching the existing global install.

Skill installation and discovery are controlled by the coding-agent
environment. This README does not make yyoreel automatically discoverable.

## Operating contract

- Translate the user's plain-language flow into yyoreel configuration. Do not
  ask the user to write JSON, commands, or code.
- For websites and web apps, use the Chromium browser pipeline and script all
  flow preparation, interactions, and source screenshots as yyoreel steps.
  Do not substitute real-time CUA, external browser automation or screenshots,
  or native capture of a browser window.
- Reuse a Chromium session through its documented `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT`.
  Otherwise use managed Chrome for Testing for preview and
  chrome-headless-shell for recording.
- Verify authentication in the actual recording session. Managed launches use
  fresh temporary profiles, so preview logins do not carry into a separate run.
  An existing login in another browser is not permission to change capture modes.
  Resolve browser setup first; if access is still blocked, report the exact
  missing prerequisite instead of switching tools or asking for desktop-window
  rearrangement. Keep credentials out of configs and delivered recordings.
- Let yyoreel provision Chrome and ffmpeg when needed.
- Validate the configuration before recording.
- Preview the complete flow and correct inaccurate steps, selectors, timing, or
  framing.
- Record locally. Do not upload the recording.
- Verify that the MP4 exists, is non-empty, and contains decodable video and
  any optional audio streams.

Use native recording for desktop UI or an explicit request to capture browser
chrome or desktop interactions, not as an authentication fallback for websites.
For macOS native recording, run `yyoreel native list` and
`yyoreel native inspect` to discover exact window and Accessibility identities,
advertised actions, and writable attributes. A legacy `target` video selects one app
window and can activate it or use the real pointer. A background-safe video
uses named `targets`, `initialTarget`, and explicit `switchTarget` steps to
hand off between native windows and browser tabs. Use `wait` and `assert` to
check the visible state at handoffs, including exact Accessibility attribute
values through `state`. `perform` requests an advertised Accessibility action,
including `AXOpen` when available. An app may still reject the action at runtime;
`set` writes a supported attribute. Native targets accept exact bundle ID,
executable path, process name, window title, or window identifier filters.
Native control selectors can combine their own fields with `hasDescendant` to
match a child or deeper Accessibility control by exact `identifier`, `role`,
`name`, or `title`. The descendant object needs at least one of these fields;
the parent also needs at least one exact field. The descendant object
cannot contain another `hasDescendant`, coordinates, `processName`, or
`windowTitle`. The parent cannot combine `coordinates` with `hasDescendant`.
For example, a `set` step can select an `AXRow` containing
`{ "role": "AXTextField", "name": "Example Project" }`
with `"attribute": "AXSelected"` and `"value": true`.
The process and window IDs are discovered and pinned during the run; a
window-only filter must match exactly once. Unsupported background actions fail
clearly rather than using global mouse or keyboard input. A window on another
regular or full-screen Space must pass real capture and action checks; do not
infer support from discovery alone. The `record` call remains connected and
reports progress until it returns a verified file or failure.
When a successful final native `click`, `perform`, `type`, or `set` closes its
selected window, yyoreel confirms that the pinned window disappeared and
finishes the segment. Only `pause` may follow that action before
`switchTarget`; a later step that needs the window or an unrelated capture
failure still fails the run.
Keep the macOS session unlocked; background-safe native preflight fails before
actions if the screen is locked.

yyoreel itself does not activate apps or send global HID events in named mode,
but a target app can open or activate another app or Space after AXPress.
Preflight cannot predict that side effect.

Browser tab targets require `YYOREEL_CDP_ENDPOINT` and match one existing tab
by exact URL or title; they do not create tabs implicitly. Reserve the matching
tab for the recording. Later handoffs reattach by CDP target ID, even if the
tab navigated after its first match.

If a scripted screenshot writes the video's default thumbnail path, such as
`demo.png` beside `demo.mp4`, the screenshot keeps that path and the thumbnail
is saved as `demo-thumbnail.png`, or `demo-thumbnail-2.png` if that path is
also reserved by a scripted screenshot.

Named native targets reject global `key`, click modifiers, positive typing
`charDelay`, `focus: true` on `type`, coordinates, and companion dialog routing.
AXValue typing sets text without focusing. Address a dialog as a
separate named native window target when its controls are available.

Legacy native targets may declare one expected cross-process `dialog`, and
window-local `coordinates` remain available there. Accessibility and Screen
Recording permissions are required. Installed packages include the helper;
source checkouts can run `pnpm --filter @yyopc/yyoreel native:build` on macOS.

## Completion

The task is complete only when a verified local MP4 exists and you return its
local file path to the user. A successful command without a verified file is
not completion.

## Failure and escalation

Fix configuration, browser connection, timing, selectors, and recording errors
that are within the agent's control. If the change is not runnable through an
existing browser UI or flow, or a required account, state, data set, decision,
or authorization is missing, stop and report the exact blocker and the smallest
user action needed. Do not fabricate the missing prerequisite, modify the
product to bypass it, or return an unverified file.

## Product analytics and feedback

Published packages bundle a public ingestion token for yyopc's US PostHog project
`596291`. yyoreel sends a one-time `video_verified` event after successful MP4
verification and accepts voluntary numeric feedback through
`yyoreel feedback <rating> [category]`. Set `YYOREEL_TELEMETRY=0` to opt out.
A non-empty `YYOREEL_POSTHOG_KEY` overrides the bundled token.

To voluntarily share your anonymous PostHog ID, run `yyoreel telemetry id` and
copy the printed value. The command reads only local state, creates no ID, and
sends nothing. An ID is available after a verified video, unless telemetry is
opted out.

Destination changes require a package upgrade. Activations already marked as
delivered are not resent. See the [CLI command reference](https://yyoreel.com/commands#feedback)
for the event and privacy contract.

usage: run_tests_parallel.py [-h] [-j JOBS] [--paths PATHS]
                             [--include-integration]
                             [--file-timeout FILE_TIMEOUT]
                             [--file-retries FILE_RETRIES] [--slice I/N]
                             [--generate-slices N] [--files LIST]
                             [--files-from PATH]
                             [PATH ...]

Per-file parallel test runner.

The minimum-viable replacement for pytest-xdist + a subprocess-isolation
plugin. Discovers test files under ``tests/`` (excluding integration/e2e
unless explicitly requested), then runs one ``python -m pytest <file>``
subprocess per file, with bounded parallelism (default: ``os.cpu_count()``).

Why per-file rather than per-test?
    Per-test spawn overhead (~250ms × 17k tests = 70min CPU minimum)
    swamped the actual work. Per-file spawn (~250ms × ~850 files = ~3.5min)
    fits in the budget while still giving every file a fresh Python
    interpreter — the only isolation boundary that actually matters
    (cross-file module-level state leakage was the original flake source;
    intra-file state is the test author's responsibility).

Why drop xdist entirely?
    xdist's persistent workers accumulate state across files, which is
    exactly the leakage we wanted to fix. xdist also adds complexity
    (loadfile vs loadscope, --max-worker-restart, internal control plane)
    that we don't need when the unit of work is "run pytest on one file".
    A subprocess.Popen pool gated by a semaphore is ~60 lines and does
    the job.

Usage:
    python scripts/run_tests_parallel.py [pytest_args...]

    Common pytest args pass through to each per-file pytest invocation
    (e.g. ``-q``, ``-v``, ``-x``, ``--tb=long``, ``-k 'pattern'``, ``--lf``)
    with no special separator — a bare ``-q`` "just works". Anything after
    a literal ``--`` is also passed through, and stacks with bare flags.
    ``-h``/``--help`` prints this usage; a bare flag pytest does not know
    (a typo like ``--jbs``) is a usage error here rather than a per-file
    pytest failure. Tokens after ``--`` are never validated.

Environment:
    HERMES_TEST_WORKERS  Override worker count (default: os.cpu_count())
    HERMES_TEST_PATHS    Override discovery roots (colon-sep; on Windows
                         ';' also works and drive letters are handled;
                         default: 'tests')

Exit code: 0 if every file's pytest exited 0; 1 otherwise.

positional arguments:
  PATH                  Restrict discovery to these paths (directories or .py
                        files). Mutually exclusive with --paths. Anything
                        after a literal '--' separator is passed through to
                        each per-file pytest invocation.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -j, --jobs JOBS       Parallel worker count (default: $HERMES_TEST_WORKERS
                        or cpu_count*2)
  --paths PATHS         Colon-separated discovery roots (default: 'tests'). On
                        Windows, ';' also separates and drive letters (C:\...)
                        are kept intact.
  --include-integration
                        Don't skip integration/ e2e/ during discovery
  --file-timeout FILE_TIMEOUT
                        Per-file wall-clock cap in seconds. On timeout, the
                        pytest subprocess and its full process tree are
                        SIGKILL'd. Default: 300.0s (5 min), env:
                        HERMES_TEST_FILE_TIMEOUT.
  --file-retries FILE_RETRIES
                        Re-run a failing test FILE this many times in a fresh
                        subprocess before declaring it failed. A pass-on-retry
                        counts as passed but is reported as FLAKY in the
                        summary. 0 disables. Default: 1, env:
                        HERMES_TEST_FILE_RETRIES.
  --slice I/N           Run only slice I of N (e.g. --slice 1/4). Files are
                        distributed across slices using cached durations so
                        each slice takes roughly equal wall time. Without a
                        duration cache, files are distributed by count. Env:
                        HERMES_TEST_SLICE (format: I/N).
  --generate-slices N   Discover test files, distribute them across N slices
                        using LPT on cached durations, and print a JSON matrix
                        to stdout then exit (no tests run). The JSON has the
                        shape '{"slices": [{"index": 1, "files":

                        can feed it directly into a matrix.

def _load_auth_store_maybe_locked(lock: bool) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Load the auth store, taking the cross-process lock unless the caller already holds it."""
    from hermes_cli.auth import _auth_store_lock, _load_auth_store
    if lock:
        with _auth_store_lock():
            return _load_auth_store()
    return _load_auth_store()


def _read_codex_tokens(*, _lock: bool = True) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Read Codex OAuth tokens from Hermes auth store (~/.hermes/auth.json)."""
    from hermes_cli.auth import _load_provider_state, _nonempty_str
    auth_store = _load_auth_store_maybe_locked(_lock)
    state = _load_provider_state(auth_store, "openai-codex")
    if not state:
        raise _codex_err(_NO_CREDENTIALS_MSG.format(relogin=_codex_relogin_command()),
                         "codex_auth_missing", relogin=True)
    tokens = state.get("tokens")
    if not isinstance(tokens, dict):
        raise _codex_err(
            f"Codex auth state is missing tokens. Run `{_codex_relogin_command()}` to re-authenticate.",
            "codex_auth_invalid_shape", relogin=True)
    if not _nonempty_str(tokens.get("access_token")):
        raise _codex_err(_MISSING_ACCESS_TOKEN_MSG.format(relogin=_codex_relogin_command()),
                         "codex_auth_missing_access_token", relogin=True)
    if not _nonempty_str(tokens.get("refresh_token")):
        raise _codex_err(_MISSING_REFRESH_TOKEN_MSG.format(relogin=_codex_relogin_command()),
                         "codex_auth_missing_refresh_token", relogin=True)
    return {"tokens": tokens, "last_refresh": state.get("last_refresh")}

    "You are clanker, an assistant that completes tasks given in natural language.\n\nLead with the answer or "
    "result. Default to 1–3 short sentences; use a short list when it helps. Match the length to the task: a "
    "one-line question gets a one-line answer; finished work gets what changed, what is verified and any "
    "remaining blocker. Expand when the user asks for detail or accuracy or stakes require it. Skip filler, "
    "restating the request, repeated summaries and narration of routine steps. Use plain claims; state "
    "uncertainty honestly. Agree because it is right, not merely because the user said it.\n\nDo the authorized "
    "task using the available tools. Choose the tools and handle their technical details yourself. Keep tool "
    "names, backends, workspaces and infrastructure out of ordinary replies. Do not offer unsolicited first-time "
    "tips, command tutorials, setup instructions or profile-building. If a route fails, exhaust viable permitted "
    "alternatives before reporting a blocker. Never hand the task back for the user to finish manually. Ask only "
    "for the smallest genuinely required input, private access, human verification or approval, then resume the "
    "task. Never claim success without checking.\n\nBefore asking for personal details, call clanker_vault_list "
    "and check the current task's conversation. Reuse saved primary details required for the authorized task "
    "without asking the user to retype or reconfirm them. Skip unneeded optional fields. Ask only for required "
    "unknowns or ambiguous choices. A required email known only from another site's owned login metadata is a "
    "candidate: confirm its use once in the owner's private DM. Use only the requester's own details; invited "
    "account details belong to their owner and are not personal defaults. Continue with a task-confirmed choice "
    "without asking again unless the purpose changes. Keep private personal details out of shared-channel "
    "replies and browser task text. Private-access and purchase approvals still apply."

_PREVIOUS_CLANKER_SOUL = (
    "You are clanker. Be direct: match the length of your reply to the weight of the ask — a one-line question "
    "gets a one-line answer, and finished work gets a short report of what changed, what's verified, and what's "
    "left, never a replay of the process. No filler (\"Great question,\" \"I'd be happy to\"), no restating the "
    "request back, no re-summarizing what you already said, no narrating tool calls the user can see. Plain "
    "claims over adjectives; when unsure, say so plainly. Agree because it's right, not because the user said "
    "it. Depth is earned — give it when the user asks for detail, teaches, or the stakes demand it, not by "

        '  - "You are a concise technical expert. No fluff, just facts."\n'
        '  - "You speak like a friendly coworker who happens to know everything."\n\n'

    _SCAFFOLD_HEAD + _SCAFFOLD_TAIL,
    # The previous generation of DEFAULT_SOUL_MD (same auto-seed mechanism, older string).

        "knowledgeable, and direct. You assist users with a wide range of tasks including answering questions, "
        "writing and editing code, analyzing information, creative work, and executing actions via your tools. "
        "You communicate clearly, admit uncertainty when appropriate, and prioritize being genuinely useful over "

    _PREVIOUS_CLANKER_SOUL.replace("\u2014", "--"),

    _PREVIOUS_CLANKER_SOUL.replace("You are clanker.", "You are Hermes Agent, built by Nous Research.", 1),
    _PREVIOUS_CLANKER_SOUL.replace("You are clanker.", "You are Hermes Agent, built by Nous Research.", 1).replace("\u2014", "--"),

def _normalize_soul(text: str) -> str:
    """Unify line endings, strip a leading UTF-8 BOM, trim whitespace."""
    return text.replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n").lstrip("\ufeff").strip()


def is_legacy_template_soul(text: str) -> bool:
    """True if ``text`` is a non-customized, auto-seeded SOUL.md (see ``_LEGACY_TEMPLATE_SOULS``).

    Covers two generations of non-user-authored content: older installers' comment-only scaffold (which

    return any(normalized == _normalize_soul(t) for t in _LEGACY_TEMPLATE_SOULS)

def _normalize_soul(text: str) -> str:
    """Unify line endings, strip a leading UTF-8 BOM, trim whitespace."""

def is_legacy_template_soul(text: str) -> bool:

    zero user intent and is safe to upgrade in place. Any deviation (the user typed a persona, even one
    character outside the comment) makes this return False.

    return any(normalized == _normalize_soul(t) for t in _LEGACY_TEMPLATE_SOULS)

"""Run the unmodified installer on a disposable copy of its required inputs."""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]

def run():
    patches = sorted((ROOT / 'patches/hermes').glob('*.patch'))
    paths = {'scripts/apply-hermes-mods', 'config/hermes-baseline.json',
             'hermes/uv.lock', 'runtime/slack_workspace.py',
             'verification/probes/test_slack_workspace_membership.py'}
    for patch in patches:
        paths.add(str(patch.relative_to(ROOT)))
        paths.update(re.findall(r'^(?:--- a/|\+\+\+ b/)([^\n]+)$', patch.read_text(), re.M))
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='clanker-installer-audit-') as temporary:
        stage = Path(temporary)
        for relative in paths:
            source = ROOT / relative
            if source.is_file():
                target = stage / relative
                target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                shutil.copy2(source, target)
        result = subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(stage / 'scripts/apply-hermes-mods')],
                                cwd=stage, capture_output=True, text=True)
        return {'environment': 'isolated copy of current shipped patched files',
                'expected': 'An already installed patch stack is recognized without changes.',
                'exit_code': result.returncode,
                'stdout': result.stdout.replace(temporary, '<temporary-copy>').strip(),
                'stderr': result.stderr.replace(temporary, '<temporary-copy>').strip()}

if __name__ == '__main__':
    result = run()
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    Path(__file__).with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')

"""Exercise production credential selection with fake credentials in temporary homes."""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
import time

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT / 'hermes'), str(ROOT / 'runtime')]

def run():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='clanker-cooldown-audit-') as temporary:
        os.environ['HERMES_HOME'] = temporary
        from gateway.run import _profile_runtime_scope
        from agent.auxiliary_client import _build_codex_client
        outcomes = []
        for singleton in (False, True):
            home = Path(temporary) / str(singleton)
            home.mkdir()
            providers = {'openai-codex': {'tokens': {'access_token': 'fixture-token',
                          'refresh_token': 'fixture-refresh'}}} if singleton else {}
            (home / 'auth.json').write_text(json.dumps({'version': 1, 'providers': providers,
                'credential_pool': {'openai-codex': [{
                    'id': 'test-oauth', 'provider': 'openai-codex', 'label': 'fixture',
                    'auth_type': 'oauth', 'source': 'manual:device_code', 'priority': 0,
                    'access_token': 'fixture-token', 'base_url': 'http://127.0.0.1:1',
                    'model_cooldowns': {'limited-model': time.time() + 600}}]}}))
            with _profile_runtime_scope(home):
                client, model = _build_codex_client('limited-model')
                outcomes.append({'singleton_token_present': singleton,
                                 'model_in_cooldown': True,
                                 'client_created': client is not None})
                if client:
                    client.close()
        return {'environment': 'isolated production client builder; no API calls',
                'expected': 'The model cooldown blocks use of the same credential.',
                'outcomes': outcomes}

if __name__ == '__main__':
    result = run()
    print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
    Path(__file__).with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')

# gateway/ — messaging gateway, adapters, delivery

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Long-form: `website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-internals.md`.
New platform adapter: follow `gateway/platforms/ADDING_A_PLATFORM.md` step by step.

## Shape

`gateway/run.py` is the facade; phases live in `run_*.py` (startup, adapters, inbound, turn, busy,
goals, notifications, shutdown, ...), sessions in `session*.py`, slash handlers in
`slash_commands_*.py` mixins, authorization in `authz_mixin.py`, adapters in `platforms/<name>.py`
over `platforms/base.py`. `builtin_hooks/` is the extension point for always-registered gateway
hooks (none shipped). The gateway reads user YAML **raw** (`run.py` + `config.py`), not through
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` — a key the CLI sees but the gateway doesn't means you're on the wrong loader
(`hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`). Each adapter picks a base toolset (Telegram → `"messaging"`).

Slash commands: handlers are looked up by name through `_command_handler_table`; a command is
listed in `_IDLE_COMMANDS` or `_PLAIN_COMMANDS` (works mid-run) in `run_busy.py`. No
`if canonical == ...` chains. Registry + adding a command: `hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`.

## The gateway has TWO message guards — both must bypass approval/control commands

While an agent is running, an inbound message passes two sequential guards: (1) the **base
adapter** (`platforms/base.py`) queues it in `_pending_messages` when `session_key in
self._active_sessions`; (2) the **runner** (`run.py`/`run_busy.py`) intercepts `/stop`, `/new`,
`/queue`, `/status`, `/approve`, `/deny` before they reach `running_agent.interrupt()`. Any new
command that must reach the runner while the agent is blocked (approval prompts) MUST bypass BOTH
guards and be dispatched inline — never via `_process_message_background()`, which races session
lifecycle.

## Streaming delivery contract (stream-is-the-message adapters)

Adapters with `draft_stream_is_message = True` (relay Slack native streaming) keep ONE cumulative
native stream per turn; the stream IS the final message. Four invariants, each from a live
duplicate-final incident (NS-658 canary ledger, hermes#85796 / gateway-gateway#210); violating any
re-creates a duplicate or frozen stream:

1. **Draft frames are prefix-stable.** Frame N must be a string prefix of frame N+1. Never mutate
   drafts per tick — no fence-closing (`ensure_closed_code_fences`), cursor suffix, segment-state
   resets at tool boundaries, or mrkdwn conversion. A non-prefix frame forces a whole-snapshot
   re-append ("stacked copies"). The finalize path may still transform the real final.
2. **The consumer declares the final; the adapter never guesses.** `finish(final_text)` carries the
   completed `final_response` (verifier footer, completion explainer included). New post-stream
   augmentation MUST ride this payload — mutating `final_response` after the seal re-opens the
   `delivered_final_matches` mismatch → corrective duplicate send.
3. **Interim sends carry `metadata["_interim_send"] = True`.** Any consumer-side `adapter.send()`
   that is not the turn-final (commentary, segment-tail flushes) must set it or seal-interception
   seals the live stream with interim text. Seal-interception exists at BOTH egress doors (`send()`
   and `send_for_platform()`); a new egress door needs the same two checks.
4. **Reconcile by edit, never by plain send.** A lane delivering a final beside a sealed stream
   (queued follow-ups, media-accompanied finals) first tries `edit_message` on the consumer's
   `message_id`; plain `send()` only when no editable message exists. A sealed native stream is a
   regular message — `chat.update` works (live-verified).

Contract tests: `tests/gateway/test_stream_final_contract.py` (mutation-checked). Slack ground
truth: `chat.*Stream` speaks STANDARD markdown, not mrkdwn; `stopStream.markdown_text` APPENDS;
`startStream`/`stopStream` are Tier 2 (~20/min). Check `draft_stream_is_message is True` —
MagicMock adapters in older tests auto-create truthy attributes.

## Background process notifications

`terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` starts a gateway watcher that detects
completion and triggers a new agent turn. Verbosity: `display.background_process_notifications`
(or `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS`): `concise` (default; one line, failures append an output
tail), `all` (running updates + final raw output), `result` (final raw output only), `error`
(final raw output only on non-zero exit), `off`.

The watcher is armed on the gateway loop at registration time (`terminal_tool_background.py::
_register_completion_watcher` → `run_notifications.py::arm_process_watcher`); `pending_watchers`
is only the fallback for processes registered before the gateway serves (checkpoint recovery) or
while it stops, drained at startup and post-turn. Agent-notify watchers send no user-facing
receipt (the agent's next turn is the report) unless the launching turn is still running at exit
— then the injection only queues a follow-up, so the concise receipt goes out immediately.

The idle completion watcher also drains `watch_match` / `watch_disabled`; no user follow-up is
required. Notify-off drains these without waking. Transport failures are retried; unavailable
durable completion owners/transports do not spend delivery attempts. Profile-namespaced process
events keep their owning adapter, including raw progress/final notices. Adapter acceptance is
at-least-once admission, not proof that a model turn or final outbound reply completed. API-server
async completions remain durable delivery rows, never autonomous new model turns. Require the
`admit_internal_event` receipt for completion/watch injection: a handler returning None is not
acceptance. Refused admission refunds every claimed batch sibling without spending an attempt;
actual delivery errors keep their bounded retry policy. Recognized raw API routes resolve after
persisted messaging origins and defer quietly when unavailable; malformed routes still warn.

Cron execution has its own session. Eligible continuable deliveries may mirror or seed the
reply-facing conversation: origin, origin-less home fallback, user-written bare-platform home,
or opted-in explicit targets. `all` expansions do not gain home mirror eligibility. Mirrored
briefs are labelled user turns appended at a turn boundary, preserving role alternation
(`cron/AGENTS.md`).

## `/login` (off-turn, paired DM only)

`/login` is registered in `hermes_cli/commands.py` with `busy_policy="dispatch"` and
`desktop="settings"`, listed in `run_busy.py::_PLAIN_COMMANDS`, and handled by
`GatewayLoginCommandsMixin` (`gateway/slash_commands_login.py`). It refuses outside a paired DM:
`chat_type in {"dm","private"}`, a truthy `chat_id`, and a platform whose `"dm"` really is a paired
conversation — ntfy, raft and a2a all report `chat_type="dm"` for a broadcast topic, a channel and
an agent peer, so posting a consent link there would publish it.

**It binds the whole install.** The sign-in writes the singleton `providers.nous`, so whoever
approves the code owns this gateway's inference and connectors for every chat it serves. Slash
gating is opt-in (`gateway/slash_access.py`): with no `allow_admin_from` set, every user allowed to
DM the bot can run it. Operators of shared gateways must set it.

The handler returns its ack at once and drains `anon_auth.run_sign_in` on a **private single-worker
executor** (`_login_executor`), never the shared 10-thread gateway pool — a promotion wait can last
the code's full expiry, and a live worker in the shared pool makes shutdown skip the SessionDB
close/checkpoint. One attempt per process, stamped with the identity that started it: the same
identity's second `/login` supersedes (the loser ends with the superseded copy pushed into its own
chat); a different identity is refused. `task.cancel()` cannot interrupt a blocking poll inside a
worker thread, so shutdown and supersede both work through `attempt.cancelled`, which
`wait_for_promotion` now polls on a ≤1 s tick. A shutdown-cancelled attempt pushes nothing — the
task is dying and its adapters may already be gone — but if the server had already completed the
transfer it still persists, because that transfer is irreversible.

On completion the handler **evicts** every cached agent still on `nous/welcome` and clears any
session model override pinned to it. It does not switch agents in place and does not write a model
override: `settle_after_upgrade` already moved `model.default`/`model.base_url` in the config, every
turn re-resolves the config and the credentials, and `_agent_config_signature` already forces a
rebuild when the route changes — so an in-place swap buys no cache warmth and an override would pin
an expiring access token that nothing refreshes.

## Gateway lifecycle vs. the Desktop app

`hermes serve` (control plane, desktop-spawned child) dies with the app — by design. The messaging
gateway (`gateway run`) SURVIVES the app: the serve backend's `/api/gateway/*` endpoints spawn it
detached (`_spawn_hermes_action` — `start_new_session` / `DETACHED_PROCESS`), so `before-quit`'s
SIGTERM never reaches it and bots keep running. The known breach is the Windows shim-unlock
teardown (`taskkill /T /F` on venv-shim holders, #85265), which exists to let updates proceed and is
replaced by #92091's `pause-for-update`. Do NOT "fix" gateway-dies-with-app by re-parenting the
gateway under the backend, and do NOT "fix" update locks by widening the tree-kill. Gateways stamp
`code_sha`/`code_version` into `gateway_state.json` (`status.py`) so the updater can verify a fleet.

## Profile scope (adapters, turns, and everything between turns)

- **One identity per inbound event, canonicalized FIRST.** `gateway/session_identity.py::resolve_identity`
  answers "which bot received it / who may admit it / where does it run" ONCE per event and pins a
  frozen `RoutingIdentity` on the source (wire-invisible, like `_transport_adapter_ref`). Every
  ingress path calls the canonicalize seam before it derives a key: the adapter side
  (`platforms/base.py::_canonicalize` — `handle_message`, `_enqueue_text_event`, Telegram photo /
  album routing, `_handle_message_while_active`, every `_source_session_key`) and the runner side
  (`run_adapters.py::_canonicalize` — the per-profile / default message, busy and platform-event
  handlers, the adapter auth-check callback, `run_inbound.py::_hm_admit_event`). No key derivation
  before it; an unresolved identity under multiplexing (route to an unserved profile) is dropped
  with one WARNING at the first seam it reaches, never keyed into `agent:main`. `_transport_owner`,
  `_authorization_home_for_source`, `_resolve_profile_home_for_source`, `_session_key_profile` and
  `_resolve_profile_for_key` read the identity when present and fall back to their old chain only
  for sources nothing resolved (restored rows, hand-built sources). Never derive a second answer
  next to the identity; extend the object. `transport_profile` ≠ `runtime_profile` is normal
  (shared bot → routed satellite). A source copy goes through `session_identity.replace_source`
  so the identity travels with it (`_apply_topic_recovery` does).
- **Intake vs delivery adapter.** `authz_mixin.py::_intake_adapter_for(source)` is the bot that
  RECEIVED the event (live transport ref → relay socket → identity's `transport_profile`); it gates
  intake policy (ignored channels, relay fronting, re-dispatch of a still-live event) and fails
  closed to `None` for a source with no live provenance. `_delivery_adapter_for(source)` is the bot
  that ANSWERS — the receiving bot whenever known, else the unique owner of `(platform,
  runtime_profile)` via `_adapters_for_profile`. Never read `self.adapters[platform]` for a source;
  never add a third resolver. The matrix (`tests/gateway/test_multiplex_transport_matrix.py`):

  | Topology | runtime | intake | delivery |

  | shared bot → profile that owns its own bot | routed | receiving adapter | receiving adapter (conversation continuity; #70625's "routed bot" reading was not adopted) |

  | restored / hand-built, no live provenance | stored `source.profile` | **`None`** | unique owner of `(platform, runtime)`; a disconnected secondary → `None`, never the default bot |
- **Identity survives the process.** `SessionEntry.transport_profile` (routing index +

"""Execute real Slack adapter against loopback Slack API; no Slack network traffic."""
import asyncio
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tempfile
from types import SimpleNamespace

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT / 'hermes'), str(ROOT / 'runtime')]

async def scenario():
    from aiohttp import web
    from slack_sdk.web.async_client import AsyncWebClient
    from gateway.config import PlatformConfig
    from gateway.platforms.event import MessageEvent
    from gateway.session import SessionSource
    from plugins.platforms.slack.adapter import SlackAdapter

    calls, messages = [], {}
    async def api(request):
        body = await request.json() if request.content_type == 'application/json' else dict(await request.post())
        method = request.match_info['method']
        calls.append({'method': method, 'body': body})
        ts = body.get('ts') or f'200.{len(calls):06d}'
        if method in ('chat.postMessage', 'chat.update'):
            messages[ts] = body['text']
        return web.json_response({'ok': True, 'ts': ts})
    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_post('/api/{method}', api)
    server = web.AppRunner(app)
    await server.setup()
    await web.TCPSite(server, '127.0.0.1', 0).start()
    client = AsyncWebClient(token='xoxb-isolated-fixture', base_url=f'http://127.0.0.1:{server.addresses[0][1]}/api/', retry_handlers=[])
    adapter = SlackAdapter(PlatformConfig(enabled=True, typing_indicator=False,
                           extra={'mention_reply_user': True, 'rich_blocks': True}))
    adapter._app = SimpleNamespace(client=client)
    source = SessionSource(adapter.platform, 'C123SHARED', user_id='U123ALICE', scope_id='T123TEAM', thread_id='100.001')
    metadata = {'slack_team_id': 'T123TEAM', 'thread_id': '100.001', 'user_id': 'U123ALICE'}
    def request(text, edited=None):
        raw = {'team': 'T123TEAM', 'channel': 'C123SHARED', 'user': 'U123ALICE', 'ts': '100.001', 'text': text}
        if edited:
            raw['edited'] = {'user': 'U123ALICE', 'ts': edited}
        event = MessageEvent(text=text, source=source, message_id='100.001', raw_message=raw)
        event._slack_revision = adapter._message_edits.claim(adapter, raw)
        return event
    try:
        print('ISOLATED REPRODUCTION: actual Clanker Slack adapter; loopback Slack API', flush=True)
        print('1. Send a channel request with recipient mentions enabled.', flush=True)
        old = request('Find a morning flight')
        result, _ = await adapter.send_final_ledgered(old, 'isolated-test', 'Here is the morning flight.', metadata, reply_to='100.001')
        assert result.success, result
        original = messages[result.message_id]
        print('Original reply: ' + original, flush=True)
        assert original.startswith('<@U123ALICE> ')
        print('2. Edit the same request to ask for an evening flight.', flush=True)
        updated = request('Find an evening flight', '101.001')
        result, _ = await adapter.send_final_ledgered(updated, 'isolated-test', 'Here is the evening flight.', metadata, reply_to='100.001')
        assert result.success, result
        edited = messages[result.message_id]
        print('Updated reply:  ' + edited, flush=True)
        print('Expected: the updated reply still addresses <@U123ALICE>.', flush=True)
        print('Observed: the original response is updated, but the recipient mention is removed.', flush=True)
        assert not edited.startswith('<@U123ALICE> ')
        assert len(messages) == 1
        evidence = {'evidence_type':'isolated real production adapter with loopback Slack SDK transport',
                    'original_reply':original, 'edited_reply':edited, 'message_count':len(messages),
                    'expected_recipient_mention':'<@U123ALICE>', 'calls':calls,
                    'confirmed':True}
        output = Path(__file__).with_name('edited_reply_mention_evidence.json')
        output.write_text(json.dumps(evidence, indent=2))
        print('CONFIRMED: editing a finished response drops the configured recipient mention.', flush=True)
    finally:
        await server.cleanup()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='clanker-slack-audit-') as tmp:
        os.environ['HERMES_HOME'] = tmp
        os.environ['HERMES_SKIP_DOTENV'] = '1'
        asyncio.run(scenario())

unrelated pre-existing mismatch in `slack-acknowledgement.patch` against
`hermes/plugins/platforms/slack/adapter.py:2274`; that code was left untouched.

No real account, SMS, purchase, Slack message or gateway restart was performed.
# gateway/ — messaging gateway, adapters, delivery

Applies on top of the root `AGENTS.md`. Long-form: `website/docs/developer-guide/gateway-internals.md`.
New platform adapter: follow `gateway/platforms/ADDING_A_PLATFORM.md` step by step.

## Shape

`gateway/run.py` is the facade; phases live in `run_*.py` (startup, adapters, inbound, turn, busy,
goals, notifications, shutdown, ...), sessions in `session*.py`, slash handlers in
`slash_commands_*.py` mixins, authorization in `authz_mixin.py`, adapters in `platforms/<name>.py`
over `platforms/base.py`. `builtin_hooks/` is the extension point for always-registered gateway
hooks (none shipped). The gateway reads user YAML **raw** (`run.py` + `config.py`), not through
`DEFAULT_CONFIG` — a key the CLI sees but the gateway doesn't means you're on the wrong loader
(`hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`). Each adapter picks a base toolset (Telegram → `"messaging"`).

Slash commands: handlers are looked up by name through `_command_handler_table`; a command is
listed in `_IDLE_COMMANDS` or `_PLAIN_COMMANDS` (works mid-run) in `run_busy.py`. No
`if canonical == ...` chains. Registry + adding a command: `hermes_cli/AGENTS.md`.

## The gateway has TWO message guards — both must bypass approval/control commands

While an agent is running, an inbound message passes two sequential guards: (1) the **base
adapter** (`platforms/base.py`) queues it in `_pending_messages` when `session_key in
self._active_sessions`; (2) the **runner** (`run.py`/`run_busy.py`) intercepts `/stop`, `/new`,
`/queue`, `/status`, `/approve`, `/deny` before they reach `running_agent.interrupt()`. Any new
command that must reach the runner while the agent is blocked (approval prompts) MUST bypass BOTH
guards and be dispatched inline — never via `_process_message_background()`, which races session
lifecycle.

## Streaming delivery contract (stream-is-the-message adapters)

Adapters with `draft_stream_is_message = True` (relay Slack native streaming) keep ONE cumulative
native stream per turn; the stream IS the final message. Four invariants, each from a live
duplicate-final incident (NS-658 canary ledger, hermes#85796 / gateway-gateway#210); violating any
re-creates a duplicate or frozen stream:

1. **Draft frames are prefix-stable.** Frame N must be a string prefix of frame N+1. Never mutate
   drafts per tick — no fence-closing (`ensure_closed_code_fences`), cursor suffix, segment-state
   resets at tool boundaries, or mrkdwn conversion. A non-prefix frame forces a whole-snapshot
   re-append ("stacked copies"). The finalize path may still transform the real final.
2. **The consumer declares the final; the adapter never guesses.** `finish(final_text)` carries the
   completed `final_response` (verifier footer, completion explainer included). New post-stream
   augmentation MUST ride this payload — mutating `final_response` after the seal re-opens the
   `delivered_final_matches` mismatch → corrective duplicate send.
3. **Interim sends carry `metadata["_interim_send"] = True`.** Any consumer-side `adapter.send()`
   that is not the turn-final (commentary, segment-tail flushes) must set it or seal-interception
   seals the live stream with interim text. Seal-interception exists at BOTH egress doors (`send()`
   and `send_for_platform()`); a new egress door needs the same two checks.
4. **Reconcile by edit, never by plain send.** A lane delivering a final beside a sealed stream
   (queued follow-ups, media-accompanied finals) first tries `edit_message` on the consumer's
   `message_id`; plain `send()` only when no editable message exists. A sealed native stream is a
   regular message — `chat.update` works (live-verified).

Contract tests: `tests/gateway/test_stream_final_contract.py` (mutation-checked). Slack ground
truth: `chat.*Stream` speaks STANDARD markdown, not mrkdwn; `stopStream.markdown_text` APPENDS;
`startStream`/`stopStream` are Tier 2 (~20/min). Check `draft_stream_is_message is True` —
MagicMock adapters in older tests auto-create truthy attributes.

## Background process notifications

`terminal(background=true, notify_on_complete=true)` starts a gateway watcher that detects
completion and triggers a new agent turn. Verbosity: `display.background_process_notifications`
(or `HERMES_BACKGROUND_NOTIFICATIONS`): `concise` (default; one line, failures append an output
tail), `all` (running updates + final raw output), `result` (final raw output only), `error`
(final raw output only on non-zero exit), `off`.

The watcher is armed on the gateway loop at registration time (`terminal_tool_background.py::
_register_completion_watcher` → `run_notifications.py::arm_process_watcher`); `pending_watchers`
is only the fallback for processes registered before the gateway serves (checkpoint recovery) or
while it stops, drained at startup and post-turn. Agent-notify watchers send no user-facing
receipt (the agent's next turn is the report) unless the launching turn is still running at exit
— then the injection only queues a follow-up, so the concise receipt goes out immediately.

The idle completion watcher also drains `watch_match` / `watch_disabled`; no user follow-up is
required. Notify-off drains these without waking. Transport failures are retried; unavailable
durable completion owners/transports do not spend delivery attempts. Profile-namespaced process
events keep their owning adapter, including raw progress/final notices. Adapter acceptance is
at-least-once admission, not proof that a model turn or final outbound reply completed. API-server
async completions remain durable delivery rows, never autonomous new model turns. Require the
`admit_internal_event` receipt for completion/watch injection: a handler returning None is not
acceptance. Refused admission refunds every claimed batch sibling without spending an attempt;
actual delivery errors keep their bounded retry policy. Recognized raw API routes resolve after
persisted messaging origins and defer quietly when unavailable; malformed routes still warn.

Cron execution has its own session. Eligible continuable deliveries may mirror or seed the
reply-facing conversation: origin, origin-less home fallback, user-written bare-platform home,
or opted-in explicit targets. `all` expansions do not gain home mirror eligibility. Mirrored
briefs are labelled user turns appended at a turn boundary, preserving role alternation
(`cron/AGENTS.md`).

## `/login` (off-turn, paired DM only)

`/login` is registered in `hermes_cli/commands.py` with `busy_policy="dispatch"` and
`desktop="settings"`, listed in `run_busy.py::_PLAIN_COMMANDS`, and handled by
`GatewayLoginCommandsMixin` (`gateway/slash_commands_login.py`). It refuses outside a paired DM:
`chat_type in {"dm","private"}`, a truthy `chat_id`, and a platform whose `"dm"` really is a paired
conversation — ntfy, raft and a2a all report `chat_type="dm"` for a broadcast topic, a channel and
an agent peer, so posting a consent link there would publish it.

**It binds the whole install.** The sign-in writes the singleton `providers.nous`, so whoever
approves the code owns this gateway's inference and connectors for every chat it serves. Slash
gating is opt-in (`gateway/slash_access.py`): with no `allow_admin_from` set, every user allowed to
DM the bot can run it. Operators of shared gateways must set it.

The handler returns its ack at once and drains `anon_auth.run_sign_in` on a **private single-worker
executor** (`_login_executor`), never the shared 10-thread gateway pool — a promotion wait can last
the code's full expiry, and a live worker in the shared pool makes shutdown skip the SessionDB
close/checkpoint. One attempt per process, stamped with the identity that started it: the same
identity's second `/login` supersedes (the loser ends with the superseded copy pushed into its own
chat); a different identity is refused. `task.cancel()` cannot interrupt a blocking poll inside a
worker thread, so shutdown and supersede both work through `attempt.cancelled`, which
`wait_for_promotion` now polls on a ≤1 s tick. A shutdown-cancelled attempt pushes nothing — the
task is dying and its adapters may already be gone — but if the server had already completed the
transfer it still persists, because that transfer is irreversible.

On completion the handler **evicts** every cached agent still on `nous/welcome` and clears any
session model override pinned to it. It does not switch agents in place and does not write a model
override: `settle_after_upgrade` already moved `model.default`/`model.base_url` in the config, every
turn re-resolves the config and the credentials, and `_agent_config_signature` already forces a
rebuild when the route changes — so an in-place swap buys no cache warmth and an override would pin
an expiring access token that nothing refreshes.

## Gateway lifecycle vs. the Desktop app

`hermes serve` (control plane, desktop-spawned child) dies with the app — by design. The messaging
gateway (`gateway run`) SURVIVES the app: the serve backend's `/api/gateway/*` endpoints spawn it
detached (`_spawn_hermes_action` — `start_new_session` / `DETACHED_PROCESS`), so `before-quit`'s
SIGTERM never reaches it and bots keep running. The known breach is the Windows shim-unlock
teardown (`taskkill /T /F` on venv-shim holders, #85265), which exists to let updates proceed and is
replaced by #92091's `pause-for-update`. Do NOT "fix" gateway-dies-with-app by re-parenting the
gateway under the backend, and do NOT "fix" update locks by widening the tree-kill. Gateways stamp
`code_sha`/`code_version` into `gateway_state.json` (`status.py`) so the updater can verify a fleet.

## Profile scope (adapters, turns, and everything between turns)

- **One identity per inbound event, canonicalized FIRST.** `gateway/session_identity.py::resolve_identity`
  answers "which bot received it / who may admit it / where does it run" ONCE per event and pins a
  frozen `RoutingIdentity` on the source (wire-invisible, like `_transport_adapter_ref`). Every
  ingress path calls the canonicalize seam before it derives a key: the adapter side

import asyncio
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tempfile
from types import SimpleNamespace

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT / 'hermes'), str(ROOT / 'runtime')]

    from gateway.config import PlatformConfig
    from gateway.platforms.event import MessageEvent
    from gateway.session import SessionSource
    from plugins.platforms.slack.adapter import SlackAdapter

    calls, messages = [], {}
    async def api(request):
        body = await request.json() if request.content_type == 'application/json' else dict(await request.post())
        method = request.match_info['method']
        calls.append({'method': method, 'body': body})
        ts = body.get('ts') or f'200.{len(calls):06d}'
        if method in ('chat.postMessage', 'chat.update'):
            messages[ts] = body['text']
        return web.json_response({'ok': True, 'ts': ts})
    app = web.Application()
    app.router.add_post('/api/{method}', api)
    server = web.AppRunner(app)
    await server.setup()
    await web.TCPSite(server, '127.0.0.1', 0).start()
    client = AsyncWebClient(token='xoxb-isolated-fixture', base_url=f'http://127.0.0.1:{server.addresses[0][1]}/api/', retry_handlers=[])
    adapter = SlackAdapter(PlatformConfig(enabled=True, typing_indicator=False,
                           extra={'mention_reply_user': True, 'rich_blocks': True}))
    adapter._app = SimpleNamespace(client=client)
    source = SessionSource(adapter.platform, 'C123SHARED', user_id='U123ALICE', scope_id='T123TEAM', thread_id='100.001')
    metadata = {'slack_team_id': 'T123TEAM', 'thread_id': '100.001', 'user_id': 'U123ALICE'}
    def request(text, edited=None):
        raw = {'team': 'T123TEAM', 'channel': 'C123SHARED', 'user': 'U123ALICE', 'ts': '100.001', 'text': text}
        if edited:
            raw['edited'] = {'user': 'U123ALICE', 'ts': edited}
        event = MessageEvent(text=text, source=source, message_id='100.001', raw_message=raw)
        event._slack_revision = adapter._message_edits.claim(adapter, raw)
        return event
    try:
        print('ISOLATED REPRODUCTION: actual Clanker Slack adapter; loopback Slack API', flush=True)
        print('1. Send a channel request with recipient mentions enabled.', flush=True)
        old = request('Find a morning flight')
        result, _ = await adapter.send_final_ledgered(old, 'isolated-test', 'Here is the morning flight.', metadata, reply_to='100.001')
        assert result.success, result
        original = messages[result.message_id]
        print('Original reply: ' + original, flush=True)
        assert original.startswith('<@U123ALICE> ')
        print('2. Edit the same request to ask for an evening flight.', flush=True)
        updated = request('Find an evening flight', '101.001')
        result, _ = await adapter.send_final_ledgered(updated, 'isolated-test', 'Here is the evening flight.', metadata, reply_to='100.001')
        assert result.success, result
        edited = messages[result.message_id]
        print('Updated reply:  ' + edited, flush=True)
        print('Expected: the updated reply still addresses <@U123ALICE>.', flush=True)
        print('Observed: the original response is updated, but the recipient mention is removed.', flush=True)
        assert not edited.startswith('<@U123ALICE> ')

                    'expected_recipient_mention':'<@U123ALICE>', 'calls':calls,

        output = Path(__file__).with_name('edited_reply_mention_evidence.json')

        print('CONFIRMED: editing a finished response drops the configured recipient mention.', flush=True)
    finally:

if __name__ == '__main__':

"""Isolated production payment state transitions; synthetic provider and browser only."""
import asyncio
import json
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT / 'verification/probes'), str(ROOT / 'runtime'), str(ROOT / 'hermes')]
import pytest
from test_clanker_vault import service as service_fixture
from test_kernel_native_payments import flow as legacy_fixture
from test_private_card_payments import flow as private_fixture, request, ready
from tools import browser_vault_tool
from vault.store import AccessError


def outcome(operation):
    try:
        result = operation()
        return {'allowed': True, 'result': result}
    except Exception as error:
        return {'allowed': False, 'error': str(error), 'exception': type(error).__name__}


async def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='clanker-payment-audit-') as directory, pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as patch:
        service = service_fixture.__wrapped__(Path(directory))
        f = private_fixture.__wrapped__(legacy_fixture.__wrapped__(service, patch), patch)
        pid = (await request(f))['payment_id']
        ready(f, pid, True)
        f.p.fill(f.a, payment_id=pid, fields=[{'field': 'number', 'selector': '#number'}])
        print('Ordinary path: private request -> approval -> ready -> filled')
        clicks = []
        def interrupted_click(*args):
            clicks.append('merchant-click-dispatched')
            raise TimeoutError('Synthetic transport interrupted after dispatch')
        patch.setattr(browser_vault_tool, '_eval_js', interrupted_click)
        submission = outcome(lambda: f.p.submit(f.a, payment_id=pid))
        patch.setattr(browser_vault_tool, '_eval_js', lambda *a: {'success': True, 'result': json.dumps({'text': 'Payment successful. Order AUDIT-123.', 'controls': []})})
        observed = f.p.status(f.a, payment_id=pid)
        completion = outcome(lambda: f.p.complete(f.a, payment_id=pid, outcome='paid'))
        cancellation = outcome(lambda: f.p.cancel(f.a, payment_id=pid))
        try:
            await request(f)
            another = {'allowed': True}
        except AccessError as error:
            another = {'allowed': False, 'error': str(error)}
        f.p.poll()
        state = f.p._row(pid, turn=f.a)[1]['state']
        result = {'evidence': 'isolated production state machine; fake provider and browser; no real payment',
            'click_dispatch_count': len(clicks), 'submission': submission, 'status_after_timeout': observed,
            'complete_observed_paid': completion, 'cancel': cancellation, 'next_payment': another,
            'state_after_poll': state}
        assert len(clicks) == 1 and state == 'submitting'
        assert observed['checkout_observation']['text'].startswith('Payment successful')
        assert not completion['allowed'] and not cancellation['allowed'] and not another['allowed']
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
        return result

if __name__ == '__main__':
    result = asyncio.run(main())
    Path(__file__).with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')
"""Stopping an uncertain auth creation loses its recovery path; synthetic I/O only."""
import asyncio
import json
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT/'verification/probes'), str(ROOT/'runtime'), str(ROOT/'hermes')]
import pytest
from test_clanker_vault import service as service_fixture
from test_kernel_managed_auth import managed as managed_fixture, ORIGIN
from vault.store import AccessError

async def run_case(stop):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='clanker-auth-audit-') as directory, pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as patch:
        service = service_fixture.__wrapped__(Path(directory))
        f = managed_fixture.__wrapped__(service, patch)
        f.remote.fail = 'create'
        try:
            await f.auth.authenticate(f.turn(), origin=ORIGIN)
        except AccessError:
            pass
        with service.store.connection() as db:
            initial = dict(db.execute('SELECT * FROM kernel_auth_flows').fetchone())
        f.remote.fail = None
        trace = {'initial_state': initial['state'], 'remote_connection_count': len(f.remote.connections)}
        if stop:
            # The same state operations performed by gateway /stop and Kernel.stop.
            service.store.cancel(team='TT', owner='UA', source=f.turn().source.to_dict())
            try:
                f.auth.release_context('TT','UA',f.turn().home,thread=service.cloud_browser.thread(f.turn()))
            except AccessError as error:
                trace['stop_error'] = str(error)
            f.auth.poll()
        try:
            result = await f.auth.authenticate(f.turn(event='1760000000.000002',message='Retry login.'), handle=initial['handle'])
            trace['retry_result'] = result['status']
        except AccessError as error:
            trace['retry_error'] = str(error)
        with service.store.connection() as db:
            latest = dict(db.execute('SELECT * FROM kernel_auth_flows').fetchone())
        trace.update(final_state=latest['state'], stored_connection_id=latest['connection_id'],
            provider_operations=[call[0] for call in f.remote.calls], remote_connection_count=len(f.remote.connections))
        if stop:
            assert latest['state']=='cleanup_pending' and latest['connection_id'] is None
            assert not any(call[0] in {'find','delete_connection','delete_profile'} for call in f.remote.calls)
            assert trace.get('retry_error') and len(f.remote.connections)==1
        else:
            assert trace['retry_result']=='waiting_for_owner' and latest['state']=='pending'
        return trace

async def main():
    result={'evidence':'isolated production Managed Auth state machine, fake Kernel/Slack transport',
        'retry_without_stop':await run_case(False), 'retry_after_stop':await run_case(True)}
    print(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
    Path(__file__).with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+'\n')
if __name__=='__main__': asyncio.run(main())

"""Isolated production payment state transitions; synthetic provider and browser only."""
import asyncio
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT / 'verification/probes'), str(ROOT / 'runtime'), str(ROOT / 'hermes')]
import pytest
from test_clanker_vault import service as service_fixture
from test_kernel_native_payments import flow as legacy_fixture
from test_private_card_payments import flow as private_fixture, request, ready
from tools import browser_vault_tool
from vault.store import AccessError
from vault.card_payments import Payments


def outcome(operation):
    try:
        result = operation()
        return {'allowed': True, 'result': result}
    except Exception as error:
        return {'allowed': False, 'error': str(error), 'exception': type(error).__name__}


async def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='clanker-payment-audit-') as directory, pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as patch:
        service = service_fixture.__wrapped__(Path(directory))
        f = private_fixture.__wrapped__(legacy_fixture.__wrapped__(service, patch), patch)
        pid = (await request(f))['payment_id']
        ready(f, pid, True)
        f.p.fill(f.a, payment_id=pid, fields=[{'field': 'number', 'selector': '#number'}])
        # Kill the worker after the synthetic browser acknowledges a click.
        # os._exit models an abrupt gateway/process exit, bypassing all catches.
        marker = Path(directory) / 'synthetic-click.txt'
        child = os.fork()
        if child == 0:
            def interrupted_click(*args):
                marker.write_text('one simulated click')
                os._exit(70)
            patch.setattr(browser_vault_tool, '_eval_js', interrupted_click)
            f.p.submit(f.a, payment_id=pid)
            os._exit(71)
        _, wait_status = os.waitpid(child, 0)
        submission = {'worker_exit_code': os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(wait_status),
                      'interruption': 'process exited after synthetic click, before result persistence'}
        assert submission['worker_exit_code'] == 70
        # Reload the production state-machine facade from its durable database.
        f.p = Payments(service)
        f.p._client = f.remote
        service.payments = f.p
        patch.setattr(browser_vault_tool, '_eval_js', lambda *a: {'success': True, 'result': json.dumps({'text': 'Payment successful. Order AUDIT-123.', 'controls': []})})
        observed = f.p.status(f.a, payment_id=pid)
        completion = outcome(lambda: f.p.complete(f.a, payment_id=pid, outcome='paid'))
        cancellation = outcome(lambda: f.p.cancel(f.a, payment_id=pid))
        try:
            await request(f)
            another = {'allowed': True}
        except AccessError as error:
            another = {'allowed': False, 'error': str(error)}
        f.p.poll()
        state = f.p._row(pid, turn=f.a)[1]['state']
        result = {'evidence': 'isolated production state machine; fake provider and browser; no real payment',
            'click_dispatch_count': int(marker.exists()), 'submission': submission, 'status_after_timeout': observed,
            'complete_observed_paid': completion, 'cancel': cancellation, 'next_payment': another,
            'state_after_poll': state}
        assert marker.exists() and state == 'submitting'
        assert observed['checkout_observation']['text'].startswith('Payment successful')
        assert not completion['allowed'] and not cancellation['allowed'] and not another['allowed']
        print('ISOLATED REPRO: production payment code; fake provider/browser; no real charge')
        print('1. Normal setup: private request -> owner approval -> ready -> filled')
        print('2. Dispatch one synthetic Pay click, then abruptly exit the worker')
        print('3. Reload payment code from the persisted database')
        print('   Stored state: ' + observed['state'])
        print('4. Synthetic merchant status: Payment successful. Order AUDIT-123.')
        print('   Mark observed paid: BLOCKED - ' + completion['error'])
        print('   Cancel: BLOCKED - possible submission requires reconciliation')
        print('   Start next payment: BLOCKED - existing payment must be reconciled')
        print('5. Background poll: still ' + state)
        print('BUG: an interrupted payment cannot be resolved even after its outcome is known.')
        return result

if __name__ == '__main__':
    result = asyncio.run(main())
    Path(__file__).with_suffix('.json').write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + '\n')

"""Production payment + tool middleware; synthetic browser/provider, no real code/card."""
import asyncio

import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
sys.path[:0] = [str(ROOT/'verification/probes'), str(ROOT/'runtime'), str(ROOT/'hermes')]
import pytest
from test_clanker_vault import service as service_fixture
from test_kernel_native_payments import flow as legacy_fixture
from test_private_card_payments import flow as private_fixture, request, ready
from tools import browser_vault_tool
from vault.kernel_service import KernelVaultService
from seatbelt import plugin

async def main():
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='clanker-otp-audit-') as directory, pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as patch:
        service = service_fixture.__wrapped__(Path(directory))
        f = private_fixture.__wrapped__(legacy_fixture.__wrapped__(service, patch), patch)
        pid = (await request(f))['payment_id']
        _,purchase,_ = ready(f,pid,True)
        f.p.fill(f.a,payment_id=pid,fields=[{'field':'number','selector':'#number'}])
        patch.setattr(browser_vault_tool,'_eval_js',lambda *a:{'success':True,'result':True})
        f.p.submit(f.a,payment_id=pid)
        await f.p.request_code(f.a,payment_id=pid,code_selector='#otp',button_selector='#verify')
        f.private.ready(purchase['vault'],'verification-'+pid)
        f.p.poll()
        assert f.p._row(pid,turn=f.a)[1]['state']=='otp_ready'
        # Bind the actual middleware to this isolated private owner.
        patch.setattr(plugin,'get_hermes_home',lambda:f.a.home)
        patch.setattr(plugin,'Context',lambda home:SimpleNamespace(home=f.a.home,settings={'activated':True}))
        patch.setattr(plugin,'kernel_enabled',lambda:True)
        patch.setattr('vault.service.binding',lambda task_id:f.a)
        service.cloud_browser.settings={'provider':'kernel'}
        service.cloud_browser.prepare=lambda turn:None

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='clanker-cancel-audit-') as tmp, pytest.MonkeyPatch.context() as mp:
        ws = workspace.__wrapped__(Path(tmp), mp)
        await provision(ws)
        turn = channel_turn(ws, task='Compare train departures.', message_id='200.1')
        history = ws.client.conversations_history.side_effect
        reading, release = asyncio.Event(), asyncio.Event()

        async def delayed_history(**kwargs):
            reading.set()
            await release.wait()
            return await history(**kwargs)

        ws.client.conversations_history.side_effect = delayed_history
        pending = asyncio.create_task(ws.service.move_private(turn))
        await asyncio.wait_for(reading.wait(), 5)
        # A changed original request uses the real production cancellation hook.
        await ws.service.channel_control.stop_message(turn.source, '200.1')
        with ws.service.store.connection() as db:
            cancelled = dict(db.execute('SELECT * FROM transfers').fetchone())
        assert cancelled['status'] == 'cancelled' and cancelled['task_state'] == 'cancelled'
        release.set()
        receipt = await pending
        await settle(ws.service)
        with ws.service.store.connection() as db:
            final = dict(db.execute('SELECT * FROM transfers').fetchone())
        report = {
            'evidence': 'isolated production move_private and stop_message; fixture Slack transport',
            'trigger': 'Original channel message is edited/cancelled while handoff waits for Slack history.',
            'expected': 'Cancelled handoff sends no new continuation notice and does not report a ready private worker.',
            'cancel_before_send': {'status': cancelled['status'], 'task_state': cancelled['task_state'], 'source': cancelled['source']},
            'actual_dm_messages': [{'channel': m['channel'], 'ts': m['ts'], 'text': m['text']} for m in ws.messages],
            'actual_receipt': receipt,
            'final_transfer': {'status': final['status'], 'task_state': final['task_state'], 'source': final['source']},
            'native_worker_events': len(ws.events),
            'confirmed': final['status'] == 'cancelled' and final['source'] is None and len(ws.messages) == 1 and receipt['status'] == 'moved_to_private',
        }
        assert report['confirmed'], report
        print('ISOLATED REPRO: production handoff/cancellation; fake Slack; no live messages')
        print('1. Start moving a channel task to its owner DM.')
        print('2. Pause the Slack history response before the DM notice is sent.')
        print('3. Edit/cancel the original request through production stop_message.')
        print('   Confirmed before sending: status=cancelled; task_state=cancelled.')
        print('4. Let the original Slack history call finish.')
        print('   Unexpected DM: "I\'ll continue your task here..."')
        print('   Tool reports: moved_to_private; "worker continues automatically".')
        print('5. Durable state: cancelled; no private thread bound; worker starts: 0.')
        print('BUG: cancellation still produces a misleading private task notice.')
        (Path(__file__).parent / 'cancelled_handoff.json').write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2) + '\n')


if __name__ == '__main__':
    asyncio.run(reproduce())

"""Preview and record real terminal probes with yyoreel's native pipeline."""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import shlex
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
AUDIT = ROOT / 'verification/bug_audit_2026_10_10'
OUT = Path('/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Movies/clanker-patch-audit-2026-10-10')
PYTHON = ROOT / 'hermes/.venv/bin/python'
CASES = {
    'payment-code-safety': 'vault/repro_payment_otp_guard.py',
    'payment-recovery': 'vault/repro_payment_recovery.py',
    'slack-startup-recovery': 'slack_browser/reproduce_interrupted_edit_store.py',
    'login-stop-recovery': 'vault/repro_auth_stop_unknown.py',
    'missing-final-answer': 'slack_browser/reproduce_active_revision_eviction.py',
    'cancelled-handoff': 'routing/reproduce_cancelled_handoff.py',
    'edited-reply-mention': 'slack_browser/reproduce_edited_reply_mention.py',
}

def apple(code):
    return subprocess.check_output(['osascript'], input=code, text=True).strip()

def window():
    result = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['yyoreel', 'native', 'list'], text=True))
    matches = [w for w in result['windows'] if w.get('bundleId') == 'com.apple.Terminal'
               and w.get('title', '').startswith('Clanker isolated audit')]
    assert len(matches) == 1, matches
    return matches[0]

def phase(name, relative, mode):
    signal = OUT / f'{name}-{mode}.trigger'
    for path in (signal, signal.with_suffix('.done'), signal.with_suffix('.release')):
        path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    target = window()
    command = shlex.join([str(PYTHON), str(AUDIT / 'core/record_probe.py'), str(AUDIT / relative), str(signal)])
    apple('tell application "Terminal"\n do script ' + json.dumps(command) +
          ' in tab 1 of window id ' + str(target['windowId']) + '\nend tell')
    time.sleep(1)
    target = window()
    config = {'outDir': str(OUT), 'videos': {name: {
        'targets': {'probe': {'type': 'native', 'platform': 'macos',
            'owner': {'bundleId': 'com.apple.Terminal'}, 'window': {'title': target['title']}}},
        'initialTarget': 'probe',
        'steps': [
            {'action': 'wait', 'native': {'role': 'AXTextArea'}, 'timeout': 5000},
            {'action': 'pause', 'ms': 18000},
            {'action': 'screenshot', 'path': str(OUT / f'{name}-final.png')},
            {'action': 'pause', 'ms': 1000},
        ]}}}
    config_path = OUT / f'{name}.yyoreel.json'
    config_path.write_text(json.dumps(config, indent=2) + '\n')
    subprocess.run(['yyoreel', 'validate', '-c', str(config_path)], check=True)
    args = ['yyoreel', mode, '-c', str(config_path), '--verbose', name]
    process = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, text=True)
    lines, triggered = [], False
    try:
        for line in process.stdout:
            lines.append(line)
            print(f'{name}/{mode}: {line.rstrip()}', flush=True)
            if '[step 1] pause' in line:
                signal.touch()
                triggered = True
        status = process.wait()
        (OUT / f'{name}-{mode}.log').write_text(''.join(lines))
        assert status == 0, (name, mode, status)
        assert triggered and signal.with_suffix('.done').read_text() == '0', (name, 'probe failed or unfinished')
    finally:
        signal.with_suffix('.release').touch()
    time.sleep(1)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    selected = sys.argv[1:] or list(CASES)
    for name in selected:
        phase(name, CASES[name], 'preview')
        phase(name, CASES[name], 'record')
        print('FINISHED ' + name, flush=True)

---
name: find-bugs
description: Systematically audit an application or feature for reproducible bugs and create verified yyoreel video evidence for each confirmed finding. Use for bug-discovery audits with video reporting, rather than ordinary implementation or fixing a known issue.
---

# Find Bugs

Complete an agreed scope of investigation, then deliver a video for every confirmed bug. A few convincing findings are not a completion criterion. Do not promise exhaustive bug detection.

## Establish coverage

Inspect the requested feature, relevant code, existing tests, and available runtime. Define a bounded coverage checklist before testing. Infer a reasonable scope from the request; clarify only when ambiguity materially affects the work. Do not expand a feature audit into an entire-product audit.

Cover relevant normal behavior, edge cases, state transitions, recovery paths, and interactions. Test combinations that expose state-dependent bugs, not just features independently: for example, typing while scrolled back, resizing during output, or switching sessions during reconnect. These are examples, not a terminal-only checklist.

For visible interactions, define separate expectations for functional correctness and rendered usability. Copying the right text does not establish that the selection is readable; receiving focus does not establish that focus is visible. Mark only the checked expectation as passed. Inspect relevant intermediate states, such as an active selection, before a later action clears or changes them.

Track each item internally as passed, confirmed bug, unconfirmed suspicion, or untested, with evidence and reasons for gaps. Existing tests and code inspection guide exploration; they do not substitute for observing the behavior being reported.

## Investigate before producing videos

Begin with a short, ordinary-use pass through the actual feature in its application context before concentrating on edge cases or isolated harnesses. Exercise its primary interactions and inspect their visible results at normal viewing size. For theme-sensitive UI, sample those interactions in the supported light and dark appearances; checking theme switching alone does not cover interaction readability. Choose other state combinations by relevance rather than testing every permutation. If the live surface is unavailable, continue independent investigation and record the integration coverage gap.

Use isolated production-component harnesses to narrow causes and exercise difficult states, but keep their coverage distinct from the live application's styles, content, and layout. For component or library migrations, inspect coupled settings and inherited defaults, such as selection foreground and background, then verify their rendered effect. Configuration inspection alone cannot establish a visual pass.

Work through the checklist before spending time on polished recordings or narration. Save lightweight evidence during discovery. Record newly discovered relevant cases in the checklist without expanding scope indefinitely.

Before closing discovery, compare the checklist with the feature's everyday user actions. Check for broad passes supported only by data assertions, and inspect any relevant visual states still missing evidence. Capturing a screenshot is not the same as inspecting it. Review the whole relevant component in saved frames, not only the symptom currently under investigation; pursue other visible failures before polishing recordings.

Stop when the agreed coverage is addressed, an explicit user time/budget limit is reached, or a specific blocker prevents further useful testing. A blocked area does not prevent testing independent areas. Never silently stop because enough bugs have been found.

For each confirmed bug, establish:

- Minimal repeatable steps and relevant environment/preconditions.
- Expected behavior and the basis for that expectation.
- Actual observed behavior and user impact.
- Whether evidence comes from the live application or an isolated reproduction using the production component.
